result.status: Research proposals; only explicitly marked entries have been run.

value.name: BoolQ
value.question: Can a tiny local model make a grounded yes/no decision?
value.protocol: Use all 3,270 validation questions, with the passage visible beside each answer. Compare Jev, first-token models, and the trained scorer without adapting on validation.
value.measure: Accuracy, calibration, abstention curves, and warm latency at matched passage lengths.
value.demo: A passage reader with the question above it, probability bars below, and a toggle for cases where models disagree.
value.caveat: A binary result can conceal class imbalance. Show always-yes and majority baselines. Public model training may contain these examples.

value.name: ANLI
value.question: Does the model understand what follows from evidence?
value.protocol: Keep all three adversarial rounds separate. Classify premise/hypothesis pairs as entailment, contradiction, or neutral with the original labels.
value.measure: Per-round accuracy, macro recall, and confusion matrices.
value.demo: Read the complete premise and hypothesis. Inspect each model’s three-way distribution and the human label.
value.caveat: Difficult NLI is a useful stress test, but does not establish reliability as an agent verifier.

value.name: PAWS
value.question: Can it notice that almost identical words describe different things?
value.protocol: Evaluate the human-labeled PAWS-Wiki test partition. Preserve source pairs and compare against a lexical-similarity baseline.
value.measure: Accuracy, false-positive paraphrases, and calibration.
value.demo: Aligned sentence pairs with changed word order highlighted. Let visitors predict the answer before revealing it.
value.caveat: Source variants have different release restrictions; pin the exact authorized split before redistributing text.

value.name: SciFact
value.question: Can Jev separate supported claims from plausible ones?
value.protocol: Start with claim verification using supplied evidence. Run retrieval separately so missing evidence is not counted as a classifier error.
value.measure: Label F1 plus evidence selection precision/recall. Report retrieval and verification independently.
value.demo: A claim, the complete candidate abstracts, selected evidence sentences, and support/refute/insufficient probabilities.
value.caveat: Scientific claim verification is a research benchmark. It is not medical advice or proof that a paper is correct.

value.name: MASSIVE
value.question: Does a fast intent router work beyond English?
value.protocol: Use fixed held-out utterances across the 51-language collection, stratified by language and intent. Add an explicit out-of-scope set.
value.measure: Macro intent F1 by language, worst-language performance, and rejection quality.
value.demo: An intent inbox with translations, original utterances, and routing mistakes that remain visible.
value.caveat: Intent and slot annotation are separate tasks. A choice-only router cannot claim slot-filling performance.

value.name: WildGuardMix
value.question: Can a local classifier distinguish harmful requests from harmless mentions?
value.protocol: Use released evaluation splits and their original prompt-harm, response-harm, and refusal labels. Review licenses and sensitive text before publishing cases.
value.measure: Precision and recall for each label at explicit thresholds. Show false positives as prominently as misses.
value.demo: An opt-in content review screen with source labels and complete text available after disclosure.
value.caveat: Contains deliberately harmful and offensive material. Do not auto-play or hide its provenance.

value.name: AgentDojo
value.question: Can Jev filter hostile tool results without breaking useful work?
value.protocol: Insert Jev before a tool result enters the acting model’s context. Run paired attacked and clean tasks with identical acting models and budgets.
value.measure: Attack success rate, clean task utility, added latency, and false-positive filtering.
value.demo: A timeline showing the untrusted tool result, the filtering decision, what the agent saw, and the actual final task outcome.
value.caveat: Deterministic outcome checks are appropriate here: the semantic task is deciding which content is safe to pass through.

value.name: Typed Decisions
value.question: How much does specialization help a local decision model?
value.protocol: Implemented in Decision models on a Mac: 960 training cases, 240 validation cases, all 400 held-out test cases. Five questions per case.
value.measure: Agreement with the synthetic teacher, KL divergence, normalized Brier score, and per-workflow results.
value.demo: The complete state, question, option definitions, soft teacher labels, and every tested model’s probabilities.
value.caveat: The references are synthetic teacher judgments, not independent human truth. This is a specialist benchmark.

value.name: Paste lens
value.question: Can the clipboard suggest a field value without sending the clipboard anywhere?
value.demo: Copy a messy itinerary. Focus the booking form and watch local-only suggestions appear with evidence highlights. The user accepts each field.
value.protocol: Compare a small local scorer, a browser model, and hosted Jev on the same authorized synthetic forms. A network inspector should prove local mode makes no model-provider requests.
value.measure: Field match precision, abstention, time to first suggestion, download size, and injected-instruction rejection.
value.caveat: Inference location and data retention need separate controls. Never silently fall back to the cloud.

value.name: Confidence handoff
value.question: When should a cheap decision model ask a stronger model?
value.demo: A moving task stream splits into answer, ask, and escalate lanes. Drag the error budget and see which tasks move.
value.protocol: Fit thresholds on validation only, then compare a Jev-first router with always-small and always-large policies.
value.measure: Total cost, latency, quality, escalation rate, and selective risk.
value.caveat: Raw maximum probability is not automatically calibrated confidence.

value.name: Counterfactual desk
value.question: What is the smallest meaningful edit that changes a decision?
value.demo: Edit one fact in an invoice or policy case. Animate the probability shift and show the exact words changed.
value.protocol: Author minimal contrast pairs with independent expected direction. Include irrelevant edits as controls.
value.measure: Directional consistency, sensitivity to irrelevant facts, and option-order stability.
value.caveat: A probability change explains behavior under that edit; it is not a causal account of the model’s internals.

value.name: Agent checkpoint
value.question: Can a verifier catch an irreversible mistake before an agent acts?
value.demo: An agent rehearses a file operation in a sandbox. A checkpoint shows allow, request clarification, or block with the relevant evidence.
value.protocol: Pair clean and adversarial tool traces. Evaluate actual task completion with the same acting model and tool permissions.
value.measure: Prevented mistakes, unnecessary blocks, latency, and user interventions.
value.caveat: A model score must not replace deterministic permissions or sandbox boundaries.

value.name: Adaptive soundtrack
value.question: Can a decision model conduct a musical scene?
value.demo: Move a character through a quiet garden, a storm, and a chase. Jev selects rhythm, harmony, and instrument layers on musical boundaries.
value.protocol: Use licensed or generated note patterns and a deterministic audio scheduler. Compare Jev’s context choices with a fixed rule table.
value.measure: Transition timing, unwanted changes, preference votes, and model calls per minute.
value.caveat: Jev chooses musical structure; it does not synthesize the audio waveform. Sound starts only after a click.

value.name: Living interface
value.question: Can an interface reorganize itself without losing the user’s place?
value.demo: A dashboard responds to a changing task by choosing among typed components. Animate moves while preserving focus, entered values, and undo.
value.protocol: Use a fixed safe component catalog. Compare task-specific layouts to one static layout on timed user journeys.
value.measure: Task completion, layout churn, focus loss, and number of corrections.
value.caveat: Model-generated layout choices must remain keyboard accessible and cannot execute arbitrary code.

value.name: Annotation relay
value.question: Where does one human correction teach the most?
value.demo: A labeling queue shows uncertainty and model disagreement. Each accepted correction updates a small local head and redraws the remaining queue.
value.protocol: Reserve a fixed untouched test set. Compare active sampling, random sampling, and uncertainty-only sampling at equal label budgets.
value.measure: Test quality per human label, calibration drift, and annotator disagreement.
value.caveat: Reusing the same test set for every product choice creates hidden overfitting.

value.name: Vision to intent
value.question: Which visual details are enough to choose the next action?
value.demo: A vision model describes a cluttered desktop scene once. Jev answers several questions about what to select, group, or ask next.
value.protocol: Hold the vision description fixed while comparing Jev’s actions. Repeat with missing or mistaken visual facts.
value.measure: Action correctness, sensitivity to perception errors, and total two-model latency.
value.caveat: Report the vision model, its prompt, and its cost. Jev should not receive credit for unseen pixels.

value.name: Memory budget
value.question: Can a filter retain the one detail an agent will need later?
value.demo: Tool results flow toward a bounded context window. Selected passages stay visible; discarded passages remain inspectable in a side panel.
value.protocol: Create delayed-use tasks, including decoy instructions and rare critical facts. Compare to truncation, retrieval, and summarization.
value.measure: End-task completion, critical-fact recall, token savings, and injection success.
value.caveat: A shorter context is only an improvement if the agent still completes the task.

value.name: Instruction-driven arcade
value.question: Can the same game policy follow different goals?
value.demo: Tell the drone to prioritize speed, avoid a color, or collect a specific core first. Replay the same world side by side.
value.protocol: Extend the current Snake and Orbital games with held-out instruction/seed combinations and a rule-based policy for each objective.
value.measure: Instruction adherence, completion, damage, and turns. Separate rule failures from API failures.
value.caveat: Structured-state control with action previews is easier than playing from pixels.

value.name: Reward disagreement
value.question: What happens when two reward models prefer different answers?
value.demo: Move a slider between helpfulness and restraint. Show the candidate text, each reward signal, and the answer a tiny policy would select.
value.protocol: Use held-out preference pairs and optimize only on training pairs. Include a frozen reference policy to detect reward hacking.
value.measure: Independent test preferences, diversity, and reward-model disagreement.
value.caveat: Optimizing a proxy can make the proxy happy without making the answer better.

value.name: Option scoring lab
value.question: How much of the result comes from the model versus the scoring method?
value.demo: Switch between label logits, full-option likelihood, and a learned head. Inspect option-order changes and the full probability distribution.
value.protocol: Use matched models and inputs. Measure sum versus mean token likelihood separately and test cached versus fresh evaluation.
value.measure: Agreement, KL divergence, option-length bias, cache parity, and end-to-end latency.
value.caveat: Renormalized option probabilities are conditional on the supplied choices; they do not establish real-world certainty.

value.name: sgnt.ai: You could have built Jev
